about: Inputs for the project measurements that need a real extraction model (src/memory/engine/eval/real_project.rs, all #[ignore]). `windows` are conversation windows of one project chat, some about the project, some about the person, some both; every stored fact is classified by the markers listed here, and the printout is read by hand besides. `personal_questions` and `project_questions` are asked afterwards. `cards` are summaries of the kind a kanban worker writes when it closes a card, retained the way the dispatcher retains them; `card_questions` are asked the way the next worker of the project would ask. Markers are matched folded (case and diacritics ignored).

cards.title: Investigate the memory growth in the worker
cards.summary: Took heap snapshots of the worker at start, after 1 hour and after 6 hours. The growth comes from a Map in src/cache/users.ts that is keyed by user id and never evicted: 1.4 million entries after 6 hours. Replaced it with an LRU capped at 5,000 entries (src/cache/lru.ts). After the change the process plateaus at 410 MB instead of reaching 2.1 GB, and the hit rate stayed at 93%. I also looked at the logging buffer, the Redis client and the websocket handlers and none of them leak, so there is nothing to do there. The staging box has 4 GB of RAM, which is why the old version was killed by the OOM killer every night around 03:00. Next step, if someone wants it: expose the cache size as a metric.

cards.title: Set up CI for the mobile app
cards.summary: CI for the mobile app now runs on GitHub Actions on a macos-14 runner. Pods are cached by Podfile.lock hash, which cut the install step from 6 minutes to 40 seconds; a full run takes 11 minutes. Code signing goes through fastlane match with the certificates in the private repo mobile-certs. Every tag that matches v*.*.* uploads a build to TestFlight. Two things to know: the first run after a cache miss can time out on the simulator boot, re-running fixes it, and the free tier of minutes is not enough for more than about 40 runs a month.
